newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to set up rural telephone fund - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to set up rural telephone fund - report.

text.p: Mexico's government will fund rural telephone service when the local telephone market opens to competition in 1997, Reforma newspaper said on Thursday.
Reforma quoted the government's telecommunications director Carlos Mier y Teran as saying Mexico will set up a government fund similar to those that have been established in Chile and Peru.
He said the fund would free former monopoly Telefonos de Mexico of its obligation to expand Mexico's rural telephone service under the terms of its 1990 privatization.
"When competition comes, (Telmex) can no longer be held to such commitments because it will be at a disadvantage compared to its competitors," Mier y Teran was quoted as saying in Reforma.

He said coming competition would probably raise local telephone prices and cut long-distance prices, eliminating a traditional cross-subsidy of local telephone service by long-distance revenues, according to Reforma.

He said interconnection fees paid by new competitors to Telmex for use of its existing network would prevent costly price wars because the fees are already set for the first three years and are gradually reduced, Reforma said.
